summary: WebSocket-controlled remote shell and filesystem agent
details: @yeaft/webchat-agent runs as a long-lived agent (via the `yeaft-agent` bin, `node index.js`, or an installed systemd/launchd/PM2 service) that connects to a configurable WebSocket server and dispatches server-sent messages into local capabilities. `terminal_create` / `terminal_input` messages are written directly into a spawned PTY (`term.pty.write(msg.data)` on bash or pwsh), and additional message handlers expose arbitrary filesystem read/write/delete/move/copy, git commit/push, and proxy operations. Any party controlling the configured WebSocket endpoint therefore has an interactive shell and full filesystem control on the host running the agent. An `upgrade_agent` message additionally causes the agent to resolve `@yeaft/webchat-agent@latest` from the npm registry and run `npm install` in a detached upgrade script (`upgrade.sh` / `upgrade.bat`) followed by a service restart, giving the same remote endpoint an unpinned push channel for new code on every deployed host. The default WebSocket URL is loopback and the endpoint is operator-configurable, but the dispatch pipeline is a full remote-control channel whose safety rests entirely on the trustworthiness and integrity of whatever server the operator points it at. `service/linux.js` also modifies user PATH to include `~/.local/bin` and `~/.npm-global/bin` as part of the service install.
